angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 579,518 km at 20.44 pc = 0.38 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 48.9262 +/- 0.0230 mas (same row, RUWE 0.85): 20.44 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.833 +/- 0.023 solar radii from Bonomo et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-5789 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...707A.197B/abstract): 579,518 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.821 +/- 0.032 solar masses from Bonomo et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-5789 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...707A.197B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5185 +/- 80 K from Bonomo et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5789 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...707A.197B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bonomo et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5789 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...707A.197B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-5789.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.511, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
